answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a refundable stake plus a history of verified useful work: a newcomer must lock collateral and complete real tasks before it earns voting or reward rights. Cloning identities then costs real capital each time, so a flood of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. Like a fable about a meadow where every grazer must tend its own patch before sharing the harvest, the horizon for attackers is bounded by cost, not by how many names they can invent.
